newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TVL, FREE STATE HEAD SUPERSPORT CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TVL, FREE STATE HEAD SUPERSPORT CHALLENGE.

text.p: Transvaal have a chance to go to the top of the table in their Supersport series four-day match which begins at the Wanderers on Friday.

Ken Rutherford's men have started the season in the most positive form of any of the provinces and home advantage against traditional strugglers, Boland will make them firm favourites to record a win.

Transvaal are fortunate not to have lost their most in-form player, Adam Bacher. It would have been a close call between Bacher and John Commins as to who flew to India to replace the injured Jonty Rhodes in the national side.
As it is, Bacher, who became the first South African ever to score a century and a double century in the same match during the last round, will spearhead a powerful Vaal batting line-up.
At Centurion Park Natal will be hoping to put a disappointing loss to Border in the last round behind them against hosts Northern Transvaal.

The selectors have refused to panic and Natal will field the same team which played in that defeat at Kingsmead. Northerns will be hoping to translate the form that has taken them to the top of the Standard Bank League into the longer version of the game.

Northerns lost in two and a half days to Free State in the last round and the men from Bloemfontein will be favourites to continue their winning ways with a home tie against a below strength Western Province.
Province will be without test stars Gary Kisten, Herschelle Gibbs, Brian McMillan and Paul Adams, while Craig Matthews is still recovering from injury.
In the final fixture Eastern Province host Griqualand West at St George's Park. Kepler Wessels is the kingpin in a powerful E.P. batting line-up, but the bowling looks a little thin.

With Brett Schultz moving to Cape Town at the end of last season, E.P. have struggled to find a viable new-ball attack. On the familiar St George's Park featherbed Griquas may be able to compete on even terms, much to the frustration of Wessels and his men.
